subject: Scheduling: Technical Deep Dive — timezone overlap for SE + customer architects
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@globex.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 16:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request — technical deep dive (solutions + architects)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Globex wants a deeper technical session focused on latency patterns, routing/fallbacks, and how Redwood handles multi-region deployments. Our architects (Priya and I) will join. Ideally we need an overlap with our APAC office (Sydney) and Redwood SEs so we can cover our on-prem -> cloud hybrid questions.

High-level constraints:
- Our Sydney team (AUS) is available 09:00–12:00 AEST (UTC+10) Mon–Thu
- Our EU architects are 09:00–17:00 CET (UTC+1) Mon–Fri
- We can be flexible for a single 90 min slot that maximizes overlap with Redwood SEs in the US and EU.

Can you propose 2–3 windows next week (Mar 23–26) that work for your SEs? Also, any thoughts on daylight savings affecting times (we have EU DST starting Mar 29, so not this week) would be helpful.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Cloud Architect
Globex Corporation

--
Alex Wu

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@globex.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@globex.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 18:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — technical deep dive (solutions + architects)

Hi Alex — great to hear, and glad the demo landed.

We can absolutely run a 90-min technical deep dive. Quick notes: US DST started Mar 8 (so our US folks are on PDT/EDT depending on region). EU is still on standard time until Mar 29, so conversions this week are:
- PDT (US West) = UTC-7
- EDT (US East) = UTC-4
- CET (EU) = UTC+1
- AEST (Sydney) = UTC+10

To avoid confusion I'll propose windows in UTC with local conversions. Proposed 90-min windows (all listed as start times):
1) 2026-03-24 00:00–01:30 UTC -> US West: 17:00–18:30 PDT (Mar 23), US East: 20:00–21:30 EDT (Mar 23), EU: 01:00–02:30 CET (Mar 24), Sydney: 11:00–12:30 AEST (Mar 24)
2) 2026-03-24 02:00–03:30 UTC -> US West: 19:00–20:30 PDT (Mar 23), US East: 22:00–23:30 EDT (Mar 23), EU: 03:00–04:30 CET (Mar 24), Sydney: 13:00–14:30 AEST (Mar 24)
3) 2026-03-24 06:00–07:30 UTC -> US West: 23:00–00:30 PDT (Mar 23), US East: 02:00–03:30 EDT (Mar 24), EU: 07:00–08:30 CET (Mar 24), Sydney: 17:00–18:30 AEST (Mar 24)

Sean/Vivek — are any of these workable for the SE team? We can rotate who leads (network/livetail+ops) depending on focus. I've attached a draft agenda and timezone grid.

Alex/Priya — if none of the above work, please tell me which local windows (in your local times) create the best overlap and I'll narrow. Also flag if you prefer 60 vs 90 minutes.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-demo-agenda.pdf, timezone-grid.xlsx

--
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Wu <alex.wu@globex.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@globex.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — technical deep dive (solutions + architects)

Thanks — quick heads up from SE ops: option 1 (00:00 UTC / 17:00 PDT) is the cleanest for our West-coast crew; Vivek and I can cover network + routing and the runtime optimizer. Option 2 would push our East-coast folks later but still doable if Alex prefers more EU overlap. Option 3 lands smack in the middle of our maintenance window for a subset of infra hosts — not ideal.

I recommend we try Option 1 and make sure we have a recording and an ops follow-up if any infra-level items need deeper dives.

I'll tentatively hold 2026-03-24 00:00–01:30 UTC on the team calendar; Marissa pls confirm with the customer and I'll carve out the SE runbook.

-sean

From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@globex.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 08:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request — Requesting Option 1 but need minor reschedule

Marissa — thanks for the options, and thanks Sean for holding. Option 1 looks best for us, but our Sydney architects ran into a conflict: they can do 11:00–12:30 AEST but not 11:00–12:30 because they have a standing on-call overlap until 11:15. Could we shift start by 15 minutes to 2026-03-24 00:15–01:45 UTC (which converts to Sydney 11:15–12:45 AEST)?

We realize shifting is a PITA for the Redwood team; if moving 15 minutes is hard, we can do Option 2 at 02:00 UTC, but preference is to keep Option 1 with the 15-min shift.

Also attaching a quick sample of the Globex architecture diagram we want to discuss (network-architecture.png).

Cheers,
Alex

Subject: Re: Confirmed — 2026-03-24 00:15–01:45 UTC (15-min shift accepted)

Thanks everyone — good catch on the on-call overlap. Sean/Vivek: we can shift by 15 minutes; Sean confirmed the backend maintenance window won't be impacted by the 15-min shift (we validated with infra). I've updated the calendar invite and included the agenda + Globex architecture attachment.

Final details:
- When: 2026-03-24 00:15–01:45 UTC (Marissa local: 17:15–18:45 PDT Mar 23; Alex/Sydney: 11:15–12:45 AEST Mar 24)
- Duration: 90 minutes
- Goals: latency profile review, multi-region routing + fallback, on-prem connectivity checklist, post-demo action items (SLA/rollout plan)
- Action items:
  - Alex/Priya: add any topology notes to the shared doc (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-demo-agenda) — please add any specific test traffic profiles you want us to run.
  - Sean/Vivek: prepare a short ops runbook and one slide showing fallback behavior under capacity pressure.
  - Marissa: record session and follow up with notes + next steps.

Attachments now on the invite: redwood-demo-agenda.pdf, timezone-grid.xlsx, network-architecture.png

See you all then — thanks for working through the timezones.

Best,
Marissa
